newsitem.title: KENYA: Increased demand lifts Nairobi bourse index.
newsitem.headline: Increased demand lifts Nairobi bourse index.

text.p: Increased demand on key shares lifted the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share index marginally on Wednesday, brokers and bourse officials said.
The index gained 1.79 points to stand at 3039.80. Turnover was posted at 9.030 million shillings traded on 243,385 shares from 9.273 million shillings on 284,911 shares on Tuesday.
A bourse official said the market was stable as prices of key shares struggled to recover.
Kenya Airways traded 50,710 shares at 55.50 unchanged, while foreigners bought 50,000 shares of Kenya Commercial Bank at between 55.75 and 56 and 48,000 shares of Kenya Breweries at at 50.
Brokers said foreign investors had placed large orders for Kenya Commercial Bank and would continue buying until they were filled.
On average Kenya Commercial Bank trades about 10,000 shares daily.
Some said Kenya Breweries was attracting interest because it was currently trading cum-dividend. Final dividend announced on September 20 was 3.50.
Oil concern Total Kenya which has been quiet for some time traded 11,500 shares at 68.50.
"The market is depressed, otherwise there should be no reason for the apparent lack of interest in Total Kenya," a senior broker said.
National Bank of Kenya traded at 14.50 unchanged, Kakuzi was at 96.50 and Kenya Power & Lighting traded 288 shares at 130 unchanged.
